analyst_view.overall: Early view: Amed (3rd, 23 pts) have scored 28 goals, one fewer than Fenerbahce, and lost only 4-3 at leaders Galatasaray, a result that ended an eight-game unbeaten run. Recep Ucar's Rizespor won at home for the first time this season just before the break (2-1 against Erzurumspor) but have scored only 13 and are without midfielder Can Bozdogan after ankle surgery. Samuel Ballet missed the Galatasaray game through a red-card ban; whether he is back here needs checking nearer the time.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, which I think is too high. Amed's games are open, but Rizespor's eleven matches have produced 29 goals in total and they drew 0-0 at Kocaelispor two weeks ago, so 4.1 would need Besnik Hasi's side to finish at an unusually high rate even at home.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners and I lean higher. Amed won six corners even away at Galatasaray and are dangerous from dead balls (Dia Saba scored from a free kick there), so at home against a side likely to defend deep they should beat their 4.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean slightly higher because Amed's discipline has slipped lately: Ballet served a red-card ban and Rayan Raveloson, Gift Orban and David Bates were all booked at Galatasaray, while Rizespor will need to stop Amed's counter-attacks.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots with Amed taking most of them. That fits: Amed had 14 shots even at RAMS Park, and Rizespor captain Taylan Antalyali admitted after the Trabzonspor game that they conceded three in eight minutes, so they do give chances away.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Amed put five on target at Galatasaray and should manage more at home, while Rizespor rarely test keepers, so I keep it near the number; it is the conversion behind the 4.1-goal forecast I doubt, not the volume.
